precepts.text: This is the wisdom Samuel applied, and the wisdom we have to learn to apply. Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. Though he humble himself and go crouching: is that not exactly what Agag did, coming delicately? Yet take good heed and beware of him; thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away. When we apply what the scriptures show us, we learn that our enemies have been the same from day one, and they are not going to change.
precepts.point: Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. Agag came unto him delicately, crouching and speaking softly, and Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

precepts.why:
Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. “Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately.” He came crouching and speaking softly: “Surely the bitterness of death is past.” And Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord: “Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.”

This is the wisdom Samuel applied, and the wisdom we have to learn to apply: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.”

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: is that not exactly what Agag did, coming delicately? “Yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.”

The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning. Esau does not forget, but we do, because we are not tapped into the scriptures. When we apply what the scriptures show us, we learn that our enemies have been the same from day one, and they are not going to change. That is the perpetual hatred we never learned.

precepts.text: God says never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness; it will surely come to pass. Though he humble himself and go crouching: he's nice to you, you got that promotion you wanted, you got that house at a discount; yet take good heed and beware of him. Thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away; the rust represents his wickedness, it's still there. Set him not by thee, lest when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place: that's what happened historically. We set them by us at the end of the dark ages, and they conquered us and took our place as Jews and Christians.
precepts.point: Though he spare it and forsake it not: it's still there. You go, no, he or she's not like that, I know them, these is good white folks, I just got a promotion, they helped me get a discount on a new car. It is still there.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Job 20:12-13 says “Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue; Though he spare it, and forsake it not”. This white man loves wickedness, and he hid it for almost sixty years. From the civil rights era up until this new administration, you saw a new America: they loved black and brown people, we got jobs, we reached the heights of government, even President Barack Hussein Obama. Then the new administration came in and said, you're fired, you're fired. DEI, get out. Affirmative action, no more. Howard University dropped 52 incoming freshmen, and over 3,000 black women in high-ranking positions were fired. This is not a new America; it's the old America coming back.

So God says, “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” It will surely come to pass. “Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: he's nice to you, you got the promotion you wanted, you got that house at a discount, they helped you get a discount on a new car. You say, no, these are good white folks, I know them. “yet take good heed and beware of him”.

“and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” The rust represents his wickedness. It's still there, kept still within his mouth, just as Job says.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place”. That is what happened historically. We set them by us at the end of the dark ages, and they conquered us and took our place as the Jews and the Christians. Even the records show it: the Arab historians and geographers, who were black Jews that spoke Arabic, wrote of black Jewish communities in Africa, the land of the Hebrews between Abyssinia and Congo and the Jews on both sides of the river Niger, and Esau asked, is this real or imagined, and wrote them down as imagined. He stood up in our place.

precepts.text: Now it gives a name to this wicked man: never trust thine enemy. But in order to understand this, you must be able to identify who the enemy is. You know what black people do? You're my enemy, you're my enemy. They'll never look at their oppressor and say that white man enslaved us, that's the enemy. Though he humble himself and go crouching: he's nice to you today; they smile with that plastic smile in your face. The white man gave me a raise. That don't mean nothing; they had a budget. Affirmative action? They get rid of that too, thanks to that negro Clarence Thomas. He became a judge based on affirmative action; now he getting rid of that thing. He said, I made mine, now I'm ending it. Thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away: like a looking glass covered with dust that you wipe; now you can see through the glass. That wickedness from verse 10 is still with him. Set him not by thee, lest when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place: that's what we did. The black Jews wanted to fight against the Muslims; we went to the Caucasus Mountains and said, we need the help of the Khazars. Those are the wildlings, by the way, in Game of Thrones. They converted to Judaism, they joined our army, we set them by us all over through our military. Now he's the Jew and you're the Gentile; he's the Christian and you're the Gentile. That's what happened. Neither let him sit at thy right hand, lest he seek to take thy seat: you ever notice when black people get in business with white folks, it'll be the black man's business, and for some reason the white man take that thing over? Remember that Edomite that had a steakhouse getting no business, and the old black dude, Tenderism, made that thing booming; a brother helped him and got it all copyrighted. Don't trust these white folks. Y'all be like, he's different, he's not like the rest. Yeah, right. And thou at the last remember my words: when they tell you to put your teeth on the curb, like American History X, now you're going to remember God's words.
precepts.point: Though he spare it and forsake it not: meaning it's still there. But keep it still within his mouth.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:

He hid the evil speech for about sixty years, from the civil rights, and now he says the time is up: we're tired of feeling bad, we ain't humbling ourselves to you no more, we're going to tell you exactly how we feel. They call it black fatigue. “Though he spare it, and forsake it not”: it's still there.

Now Sirach gives a name to this wicked man: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” But to understand this you must be able to identify who the enemy is. Black people call each other the enemy, but they will never look at their oppressor and say, that white man enslaved us, that's the enemy.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. He's nice to you today; they smile that plastic smile in your face. The white man gave me a raise: that don't mean nothing, they had a budget. Affirmative action? They got rid of that too, thanks to that negro Clarence Thomas, who became a judge by affirmative action and then ended it: I made mine, now I'm ending it. “and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” Like a looking glass covered with dust that you wipe: now you can see through the glass. The wickedness of verse 10 is still with him.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place”. That is what we did. The black Jews wanted to fight against the Muslims, went to the Caucasus Mountains and said, we need the help of the Khazars. They converted to Judaism, joined our army, and we set them by us all through our military. Now he's the Jew and you're the Gentile; he's the Christian and you're the Gentile.

“neither let him sit at thy right hand, lest he seek to take thy seat”. When black people get in business with white folks, it'll be the black man's business, and somehow the white man takes it over, like the brother who made an Edomite's empty steakhouse boom and it all got copyrighted away from him. Don't trust these white folks, even the one you think is different. “and thou at the last remember my words, and be pricked therewith”: when they tell you to put your teeth on the curb, like American History X, then you're going to remember God's words.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue”. When we got our little civil rights, there were certain things the white man could not say no more. He had to watch the name calling; he had to give us jobs. So he hid the wickedness under his tongue. But now he's not hiding it no more: all you immigrants get out of our country, the Haitians out, the name calling, DEI, it's all ending now.

Sirach is the precept: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. Though he humble himself, and go crouching”. That is him bowing down to you. Remember in DC, the police and white folks bowing to Black Lives Matter, hugging, kissing and crying, and a lot of blacks and Latinos said, see, they love us, they're humbling themselves to us. The Pope apologized for slavery and kissed feet, and the Africans said, he loves us. But did the Vatican not steal all the wealth from us and keep our records secret? Are they giving the wealth back? An apology means nothing without restitution. If I steal your wallet and I'm apologizing, I give you your wallet back.

“yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass”. You ever see a dirty glass and you wipe it so you can see? God says that is how that white man is: wipe the looking glass so you can see clear, “and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” The rust is still there. The wickedness is still there. God is saying, don't be deceived.

Job says the same thing: “Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth”. It's still there. Kramer from Seinfeld, a show our people loved and laughed through, went on a frenzy cursing black people out, that forty years ago you were hanging from a tree. The wickedness was under his tongue the whole time. They hate our guts.

precepts.text: Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. Who is the iron? That fourth kingdom. In the 50s and the 1800s you understood who your enemy was. As iron rusts, the rust will always come back: even though he said we changed, we gave you civil rights, you see the wickedness coming back now. Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away. He did not change; he is the same person, and you are seeing it today.
precepts.point: They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay. The iron mingled itself with the seed of men after 1945: Britain opened itself to its colonies, and America opened after civil rights. But God says they will not cleave one to another. White people and everybody else are not going to get along. That is what you see going on in Europe and in America.

note.label: Seeking Justice in an Unjust System

precepts.why:
The fourth kingdom “shall be strong as iron”. It began with Rome, and America and Europe are the extension of Rome, the iron of the feet. Now Sirach: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Who is that iron? The fourth kingdom that rules the earth today, Europe and America, the white man.

Who is your enemy? In the 1950s you understood who your enemy was. In the 1800s you understood. Forty or fifty years ago you understood. God says never trust him. As iron rusts, the rust will always appear again, and that is his wickedness. Even though he said, we changed, we gave you civil rights, we are not oppressing you anymore, you see the wickedness coming back now, and they are taking it all back. His kingdom is made of iron, and that wickedness will always return.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. He acts like he loves black people and cares about them. Beware of that iron. “and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” If you are righteous and have wisdom, you see all his wickedness as in a looking glass: look at their history. They are a genocidal race of people, and you cannot get justice from them. Look at Palestine, Lebanon and the Congo, hundreds of thousands dead, while the ones running the courts don't stop it. This whole system is unjust.

That is why Daniel says the iron shall “mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”. After 1945 Britain opened itself to the people of its colonies, and after civil rights everybody started coming to America. The white man said he changed, and brought the same people he colonized and destroyed to live among him. Decades later they say they should never have let any of them in. The white man did not change; he is the same person, his rust has not been wiped away, and white people and everybody else are not going to get along.

precepts.point: Then shall his mind change. After World War II America put on a new face; now it is returning to its old nature.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “they shall scoff at the kings, and the princes shall be a scorn unto them”. That is how America and Europe are: they went into Venezuela and took a sitting president. “For they shall heap dust, and take it”: dust is confusion. Say he is a drug dealer bringing fentanyl to America, and then take him. “Then shall his mind change, and he shall pass over, and offend”. Sirach warns us what that change is worth: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.”

America was always a violent people: they took this land from the North American Indians and put them on reservations, overthrew nations in South America, and went into Haiti in the early 1900s, took the gold and murdered the leaders. After 1945, when America became the world superpower and the head of the beast, it could not lead the world while still lynching and segregating openly. So it put on a new face of justice, peace and rights. That is why they gave civil rights, Section 8 and food stamps: not because they love you, but to pacify you. Now he is changing back to who he used to be. Make America great again means before the 60s.

You can shine a piece of iron and make it look good, but leave it over time and the rust appears. That is the white man's wickedness: it always comes back. “Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. In the civil rights movement he humbled himself, marched with us and said sorry for what his forefathers did, but “his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” That is why people are surprised at the KKK, the Nazi supremacists and ICE. The Constitution was written when you was a slave, and it counted you three-fifths of a man.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place”: do not make marriages with him and his woman. It happened in South Africa and in South American countries. After the civil rights era many of us forgot who the enemy was; some even have kids by him and say they love him, but God says never trust your enemy. “Who will pity a charmer that is bitten with a serpent”? The serpent is your enemy. If you go and befriend him and get bitten, nobody will pity you. We warned you.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” That sounds harsh, but it is in the Bible. We had DEI and the Civil Rights Act since 1964, and y’all thought y’all were good. Then Trump rolled it back, and Walmart, Meta, Amazon, McDonald’s all followed, every last one of them in agreement. And y’all act surprised. This is the same man who sent the National Guard so you couldn’t go to school with him, bombed little girls in a church, and bombed the all-black Wall Street. You think he loves you now? His wickedness rusts back through like iron.

Then a black man in a suit and tie on national television said that when Americans see deportations and the border closed, they will say, this is what I voted for, and Daddy’s back. The black man is in love with his oppressor; that is why we can’t win our people over. Y’all thought Diddy was bad. The white race as a collective is the real Diddy.

Isaiah names that spirit: “Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.”

That is what you just saw. Because he has a little higher position in captivity than his brothers, he makes lies his refuge and thinks the scourge will not come to him. A grown man calling the white man daddy: how is a black woman going to respect you after that? He made a covenant with death and hell, trusting the enemy that the Bible says never to trust.

It shows how near and dear the white man is to their heart. They are happy he will allow them their debauchery.

Daddy’s home. That is the Daddy in the scriptures. The chief priests rejected their own King and claimed Caesar, just as our people today reject the truth and call the white man daddy.

Then they act confused when he shows his true colors and rolls back DEI. You knew it was a snake. That is what Christianity does: you never read the Bible, you are put to sleep every week, and when you go out in the world everybody sees color except you. Open your Bible. Never trust thine enemy.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
They tell you plainly they are the evil seed, and you can believe them if you want to, but they ain't fooling us. God said: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Never trust our enemies.

Then Micah shows the enemy at work: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds!” That is Esau. In his sleep he is thinking, when I wake up, what type of evil am I going to do? “when the morning is light, they practise it”: he gets up and practises the same evil he was thinking of the night before, “because it is in the power of their hand.”

Picture it: we are going to steal the oil in Nigeria; let's say we are going in to defend the Christians. Nigeria is a black country, and if white men go in, they will be called racist. So find me a dumb black woman, the biggest hoe, one with millions of followers that dumb black people will believe, like Nicki Minaj, and put her up front. That is devising iniquity on the bed and practising it in the morning.

His wickedness rusts through everything like iron rusts. So never trust him when he says he is defending you, and never trust the peace he talks about.

note.label: 1 Samuel 22: Never Trust Thine Enemy

precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” The scriptures tell us we are never supposed to trust our enemies, yet here is Saul with an Edomite set over his servants.

“Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul.” He reported that he “saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub”, and that Ahimelech “enquired of the Lord for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.” Saul had placed his enemy over his own house, and that enemy's wickedness came out.

precepts.text: The Philistine lords understood this even without the book; it is a lesson for us to apply today.
precepts.point: This is the wisdom we have to apply today. There is always an outsider who dresses like us, talks like us, and gets himself accepted among our people; yet even the Philistines knew: he might be good to you, he might be serving you, but do not trust your enemy.

note.label: 1 Samuel 29: Never Trust Thine Enemy

precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” The Philistine lords understood this even without the book.

Achish told David, “thou hast been upright”, and “I have not found evil in thee since the day of thy coming unto me unto this day: nevertheless the lords favour thee not.” Though David was good in his sight “as an angel of God”, “the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.”

One of the things to take from this reading is that they have more sense than we do. The lords of the Philistines said, No, he cannot go to battle with us, because we will always be looking over our shoulders wondering if he is going to change his mind and go back unto his people.

This is the wisdom we have to apply today. There is always an outsider who dresses like us, talks like us, and gets himself accepted among our people. Yet even the Philistines knew: he might be good to you, he might be serving you, but do not trust your enemy.

points: Book read in class, Sails of Hope: to what extent Columbus hoped that Jewish people would be found there was a concern he locked away in the innermost recesses of his soul; but among his contemporaries the belief was slow to die, and the first voyagers and colonists looked for whatever signs might link the Indians with the ten lost tribes of Israel. When the Spaniards conquered Peru they were again disposed to look for evidence that the Peruvians were of Jewish origin. In 1607 Gregorio Garcia expressed the view that the first inhabitants of the Americas had been Jewish; in 1650 the same opinion was put forward in England; Menasseh Ben Israel, the Portuguese rabbi who persuaded Cromwell to readmit the Jews to England, shared the conviction; and Montezinos, under the name Aaron Levi, reported that in South America he had associated with Jews of the ten tribes of Israel. Scholars noted the parallels between the Indians and the ancient Hebrews: belief in a life after death, the organization of the priesthood, prophecies and dream interpretation, religious sacrifices, and the appointment of a day of rest, a Sabbath.
